svg.aria-label: A row of 119 ticks, one per pass, with 16 of them highlighted
svg.title: A row of 119 ticks, one per pass, with 16 of them highlighted
svg.text: 119 passes run when you type -O2 on a five line loop. 16 of them change the IR.
One tick per pass, left to right, in the order they ran.
52 LoopDeletion deleted the loop, no dump
The orange one is the pass that removed the loop, and it is the only one with nothing to
show you. opt prints the IR after a pass by asking the loop it just ran on to print itself,
and by then there was no loop. It writes one line instead and no IR at all.
Look at the pass before it. IndVarSimplify made the function five lines longer, which is
the opposite of what an optimiser is supposed to do, and it is what made the deletion
possible. Getting shorter is not the same thing as making progress.
The grey ticks are not wasted work either. Most of them are a pass looking for a pattern
that is not in this function, and the same pipeline has to be right for five lines and for
five thousand. Take the loop out and it drops to 108 passes with 7 changes.
Measured with Homebrew LLVM version 23.1.0 on Darwin arm64, pipeline default<O2>.
